claim:recruitment-baseline.proposition:
Responders climb the secreted gradient and are recruited to the source: the
recruitment index rises from 0 to a plateau of ~0.67-0.83 (mean approach 0.61).
claim:recruitment-baseline.hypothesis:
With the cue secreted (rate 10) and the response intact (lambda 14), responder
centres of mass move toward the source region and the recruitment index rises
well above zero.

primary_tests.name: Responders are recruited to the source

evidence_refs: Responders are recruited to the source

claim:recruitment-inhibited.proposition:
Blocking the chemotactic response abolishes recruitment: the recruitment index
stays at 0 (mean approach ~0), despite the cue being present.
claim:recruitment-inhibited.hypothesis:
With the cue present but the response inhibited, responders no longer climb the
gradient; the recruitment index stays near zero.

claim:recruitment-adversarial.proposition:
Without a cue, competent responders are not recruited: the recruitment index
stays at 0. The metric does not produce a false-positive recruitment signal.
claim:recruitment-adversarial.hypothesis:
With the response intact (lambda 14) but the cue removed (rate 0), there is no
gradient to climb; the recruitment index stays at zero.

claim:recruitment-receptor-baseline.proposition:
Cue + receptor-gated response recruits: across 5 seeds the final
recruitment index is 0.5667 (95% CI 0.3451-0.7882), above the 0.5 pass
threshold, with responder activation gated by a receptor Kd cited to
Nasser 2009 rather than a hand-tuned chemotaxis strength.
claim:recruitment-receptor-baseline.hypothesis:
With the cue secreted (rate 10) and the receptor-gated response intact
(chemo_lambda 14, kd 2.9 nM), responders whose Hill-occupancy crosses the
activation threshold chemotax up the gradient, and the recruitment index
rises well above zero, consistent with the phenomenological baseline.

claim:recruitment-receptor-blocked.proposition:
Blocking the response downstream of receptor activation abolishes
recruitment: the final recruitment index is 0.0667 (95% CI 0.0-0.1467),
below the 0.1 pass threshold, despite the cue being present and receptors
still able to bind ligand.
claim:recruitment-receptor-blocked.hypothesis:
With the cue present (rate 10) but the receptor-gated response disabled
(blocked=True), responders may still activate (naive -> activated) but no
longer chemotax, so the recruitment index stays near zero.

Receptor occupancy law with the cited Kd (evidence → mechanism)

claim:recruitment-adaptive.proposition:
A receptor mechanism that adapts its half-occupancy set-point to the
locally sensed background (fold-change detection) recruits responders
across a RANGE of background cue levels where a fixed-kd mechanism
saturates and fails: measured recruitment_index at low_bg is 0.82
(adaptive) vs 0.58 (hill); at high_bg it is ~0.56 (adaptive, mean over 12
seeds) vs 0.00 (hill, deterministic collapse). Blocking the receptor-gated
response abolishes recruitment for both (0.00), while the non-receptor
static mechanism ignores the block (0.72) -- the discriminating control
that isolates receptor-mediated gating as the necessary cause.
claim:recruitment-adaptive.hypothesis:
An adaptive receptor mechanism (a slowly-tracked local-mean set-point that
re-centers the Hill kd every SAMPLE-step increment) recruits responders at
low background AND at high background, because it senses the CHANGE in
local occupancy rather than its absolute level (Barkai & Leibler 1997;
Tu, Shimizu & Berg 2008). A fixed-kd hill mechanism recruits at low
background but collapses at high background once both sides of the
gradient saturate near occupancy ceiling. Both mechanisms are abolished
when the downstream chemotactic response is blocked, since neither is a
metric artifact -- only a mechanism that isn't receptor-mediated at all
(the static-lambda control) would ignore that block.
evidence_refs: Model-building loop — mechanism ladder (recruitment index per rung × condition)

narrative.question:
Does a secreted chemotactic cue drive directional migration and recruitment of
responder cells into the source region, and does inhibiting the chemotactic
response reduce that recruitment?

decisions.title: Should the Biological Claim Layer compiler now regenerate this study set from a hand-authored claim bundle?
decisions.detail:
This investigation is the ground-truth native realization. The next claim-
layer increment is to author the claim bundle and prove the compiler
reproduces these three studies (and their behavior contracts) from it.
